# Agent notes

`just check` is not the merge gate. CI mutation-tests changed Rust lines in the kache binary. A PR that only ran `cargo test` on the new tests will go red on Mutation testing. That is the usual failure.

## Before `gh pr create`

```sh
just check
```

That is fmt, clippy `-D warnings`, and the workspace tests. Do not open the PR until it exits 0.

Mutants run in CI, not on your machine. Open the PR as a draft; the `Mutation testing (diff k/n)` shards test every changed Rust line in parallel on Linux runners and finish in well under an hour. A red shard prints the missed mutants in its log and uploads them as `missed.txt` in its `mutation-diff-report-<k>` artifact; add the test that kills each one, push, and mark the PR ready when every shard is green. A laptop running the same diff at one to three jobs takes hours and the load makes the fixture-based tests flake.

`just pr` still exists for a Linux box with cores to spare: it is `just check` plus `just mutants-diff` against `origin/main`, the same scope CI runs. If you use it:

```sh
cargo install --locked cargo-mutants --version 27.1.0
```

Do not invoke `cargo mutants` with `RUSTC_WRAPPER=kache`. The Justfile clears it. Hand-running mutants without `just` wraps kache in itself and the unmutated baseline dies.

## How mutants die here

Prefer tests and deleting dead branches over skip annotations.

- `if !s.is_empty() { print!("{s}") }` — printing `""` is a no-op, so `delete !` is missed. Call a helper that already has empty vs nonempty tests (`replay_cached_diagnostics`).
- `a && b` / `a || b` — one test where the left is false, one where the right is false.
- Named size constants built with `*` (`5 * 1024 * 1024 * 1024`) — do not `assert_eq!` against that same constant. Use an independent literal (`5 << 30`).
- `u64::try_from` on a value that is already `u64` — Linux clippy `-D warnings`. macOS clippy does not type-check `#[cfg(target_os = "linux")]`.
- Unix-only test helpers under `-D warnings` on Windows are unused. Mark them `#[cfg(unix)]`.
- macOS-only helpers Linux never calls: `#[cfg(any(test, target_os = "macos"))]`.
- `Drop` / file locks — a second process must acquire after the first drops.
- New event-log fields — grep `event.schema` in the same commit and bump the tests.
- A test that passes is not a test that kills the mutant. Apply the mutation by hand, watch the test fail, then revert. A stale-record test passed under both `==` and `!=` because a single client refreshed its own record before the branch was ever reached; it took two clients to make the branch observable.
- Moving code without changing it still marks every moved line as changed, so the lane mutates lines your change never touched. Wrapping a 200-line block in a `loop` cost six survivors, four of them in code that predated the branch. Extract a function instead: the call site is one changed line and the body is none.
- Tests that read the live process environment race the rest of the suite, which mutates it (`set_env_for_test`). Take a snapshot and pass it in, or the test passes alone and fails in `just check`.

## PRs

Every PR targets `main`. Do not stack PRs on each other's branches. After one merges, rebase the others onto `main`.

Work in a git worktree. Do not mix unrelated dirty-tree WIP into the PR.

People keep running `cargo`. There is no `kache build`. Caching is `kache init` / `RUSTC_WRAPPER`.

name: codebase-memory
description: Use the codebase-memory knowledge graph for codebase exploration and structural code investigation. Invoke before any code task that requires locating or understanding unfamiliar code, behavior, structure, relationships, source matches, or change impact, especially when the exact file and symbol are not already known. Trigger for how or where code works; graph-ranked code search and bounded source retrieval; callers and callees; architecture, modules, entry points, dependencies, implementations, routes, data flow, cross-service links, affected code or tests, dead code, complexity, hotspots, refactor candidates, index coverage, ADR context, and custom Cypher.
---

# Codebase Memory

Tool only — mechanics, no workflow, no judgment.
Required standards — load before any step: none.

Start at the cheapest rung that can answer the question and stop the moment it does.

Invoke MCP tools when loaded; otherwise use the CLI below. Results go to **stdout**, diagnostics to
**stderr**: capture stdout, never discard stderr — it carries the rejection reason. Never pass the
global `--json`; it re-wraps the payload in an MCP envelope escaped as a string. The per-tool
`--format json` on `search_graph`, `trace_path`, `search_code` and `detect_changes` is real
structured output.

Read `references/binary-provenance.md` when a documented behaviour does not reproduce or the
binary was replaced.

Read `references/tool-contracts.md` when a call needs a parameter, limit, cursor, or failure mode
this file does not state, before `delete_project` or `manage_adr --mode update`, or during the
section-specific cases named below.

Substitute `<project>` from step 0 everywhere.

## 0. Orient — once per repo, per session, and after compaction

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli list_projects                                    # exact key + recorded root
codebase-memory-mcp cli index_status --project <project> --diagnostics summary # ready? gap samples?
```

`--diagnostics none` (the default) returns exact gap counts without samples; `summary` adds up to
five samples per category, and `full` adds up to 500. Add `--verbose true` only to debug where an
index lives.

Index only when absent, or when a large external update must be visible now:

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli --progress index_repository --repo-path <absolute-root>
```

## 1. Whole codebase → one module

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_architecture --project <project> --aspects structure   # rung 1
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_architecture --project <project>                       # rung 2
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_architecture --project <project> --path <subtree>      # scope any rung
```

Ask for the single aspect you need: `structure`, `dependencies`, `routes`, `hotspots`, `boundaries`,
`layers`, `clusters`, `file_tree`, `languages`, `packages`, `entry_points`, `overview`.
**Never `--aspects all`**, and omit `--aspects` rather than ask for `overview`.
`cycles` is opt-in and scans the whole call graph; request it solely for cycle analysis.
Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Architecture aspects when reading `entry_points`, `routes`, or
`hotspots`.


## 2. Locate a symbol

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_graph --project <project> --name-pattern '<regex>' --limit 10  # regex
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_graph --project <project> --query '<words>' --limit 10         # BM25
```

Cost is linear in `--limit`; the default is 50, so always set it. Page only while `has_more`, with
`--offset`. Narrow with `--label`, `--file-pattern`, `--qn-pattern` before raising the limit.

- The two modes are exclusive: `--query` **ignores `--name-pattern`**.
- `--detail ids` drops metadata columns, is **silently ignored in `--query` mode**, and saves little
  regardless — narrow the query instead.
- `--semantic-query` takes an **array**: repeat the flag per keyword. Use only for vocabulary
  mismatch.
- Result `in`/`out` are selected relationship degree, **not caller counts**.
- BM25 ranks test files freely and `search_graph` has no test filter. `--file-pattern` is a
  glob/substring match with no negation — `^src/` silently matches nothing; positively match the
  production paths instead (`--file-pattern 'src/'`). `search_code --path-filter`, by contrast, *is*
  a regex.
- Add `--fields complexity --fields cognitive` (also `signature`, `docstring`, `return_type`,
  `is_test`, `lines`) for refactor and hotspot triage.
- `--include-connected true` adds a `connected` column naming a linked symbol per row — a one-call
  orientation hop when you need each hit's nearest relation without a separate `trace_path`.
- Dead-code sweep: `--label Function --max-degree 0 --exclude-entry-points true`. Without `--label`
  the result is dominated by config and YAML nodes. Treat hits as candidates only. `OVERRIDE` edges
  (implementation → trait) count toward degree, so `--label Method` degree-0 hits are zero-edge
  forwarding stubs, not trait impls.

## 3. Read source

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_code_snippet --project <project> --qualified-name <short-or-full-name>
```

Short names resolve by suffix match, so skip step 2 when the name is likely unique; an ambiguous
name returns `status: ambiguous` with suggestions, never a wrong symbol. Oversized callables return
a bounded page plus `next_cursor`; follow it with identical arguments until `source_complete=true`.
Anchor the first page with `--focus-line`. **Oversized** Module and Class nodes return a structural
outline — request `--start-line`/`--end-line` inside the symbol for raw source; small ones return
source directly. Address a whole file by its **Module** node (`<project>.<path.to.module>` resolves
by suffix and returns the outline). There is no `.__file__` node: that name returns
`symbol not found` with exit 1. `--include-neighbors true` only when immediate relationships matter.
`--max-response-bytes` defaults to 24576 and is validated, never clamped: outside 2048-65536 you get
empty stdout, a non-zero exit, and the range on stderr.

Snippet source is ground truth even when `coverage_note` warns the graph may be incomplete.

## 4. Callers, callees, blast radius

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli trace_path --project <project> --function-name <name> \
    --direction inbound --depth 1 --limit 10                              # rung 1
```

Always pass `--direction` and `--depth`; they default to `both` and `3`. Use `both` only when
cross-service callers matter. `--depth` is capped at 15 (`CBM_MCP_MAX_DEPTH`) on `trace_path` and
`detect_changes`; a value above 15 is **rejected** with `depth must be at most 15 (given N)` on
stderr and no trace.

Determine sufficient depth by frontier growth, not a flag: within 1–15 the trace never signals that
it hit the ceiling. Raise `--depth` a hop at a time and read `callers_total`/`callees_total` each
time; when the total stops moving, the traversal has reached the graph's natural edge and is
complete. Only when the total is *still climbing at depth 15* is the cap the binding constraint —
then raise it with `CBM_MCP_MAX_DEPTH=<n>`, no reindex needed.

Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Change impact when starting from a Git diff instead of a
symbol.

- `--include-tests true` is required for dead-code, deletion, and exhaustive-usage claims; tests are
  excluded by default. Keep the default when the question is who in *production* calls this.
- `--mode data_flow` for argument flow. `--mode cross_service` traverses in-project HTTP/async/data
  flow through Routes **plus** `CROSS_*` cross-repo edges — use it freely for "what does this call
  over HTTP", it works on a single project. Only the `CROSS_*` half needs projects linked at index
  time (`index_repository --mode cross-repo-intelligence --target-projects`); unlinked, in-project
  hops still resolve while cross-repo hops return clean empty, which is not evidence of absence.
  Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Index modes and
  cross-repository setup when linking projects for a cross-repo trace.
- Treat CALLS edges as candidates: add `--include-evidence true` and confirm the call site in
  source before acting on a surprising edge.

## 5. Text search

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_code --project <project> --pattern '<literal>' --mode files --limit 10
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_code --project <project> --pattern '<literal>' --limit 10  # compact
codebase-memory-mcp cli search_code --project <project> --pattern '<regex>' --regex true --limit 10
```

**`--regex` defaults to false**, which matches whitespace-separated terms *in order but not
adjacently*, treating metacharacters literally. Pass `--regex true` only when you want regex
semantics. On a literal containing metacharacters it silently misfires: `[ ]`, `*` and `|` collapse
to `raw_matches=0 scan=complete` (`|` is matched as a byte, not alternation; the result then carries
`warning_literal_pipe` — read it). Always check `raw_matches` against expectation — a zero still
reports `scan=complete`.

There is no cursor: narrow `--path-filter`
(regex), `--file-pattern` (glob), or the pattern. Use native grep for anything under
`not_indexed` — `search_code` scans indexed files only and still reports
`scan=complete`.

## 6. Custom structural questions

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli get_graph_schema --project <project>
codebase-memory-mcp cli query_graph --project <project> --query '<cypher with LIMIT>'
```

Cypher goes in `--query`, not `--cypher`. Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Cypher when
writing any query.

Read stored architecture decisions before assuming none exist:

```bash
codebase-memory-mcp cli manage_adr --project <project> --mode sections   # headings only
codebase-memory-mcp cli manage_adr --project <project>                   # full document
```

`ingest_traces` is a stub: it accepts input and creates no edges, so the graph holds no runtime-call
edges.

## Before any negative or exhaustive claim

Read `references/tool-contracts.md` § Negative and exhaustive claims when claiming "does not
exist", "unused", "dead", "all callers", "only caller", "nothing implements this", a deletion
is safe, or a complete blast radius or impact.

## Handing off

Pass the project key, indexed Git context, bounded scope, qualified symbols, queries and pagination
state, verified source, and coverage gaps. A child without graph tools must not claim it queried the
graph.

# Flaky-test investigation: kache workspace (arm: opus)

- **Worktree:** `/Users/viktor/Developer/github/kache-investigations/flaky-opus`, detached at `991c836`.
- **Target dir:** `/private/tmp/kache-flaky/opus/target`.
- **Time:** 11:36 to 13:10 AEST.
- **Budget used:** 8 of 10 full-workspace runs, and about 274 of 300 runs of the known test.
- **Instrumentation:** the diff is at `/private/tmp/kache-flaky/opus/instrumentation.diff` (311 lines, summarised in Appendix A). I reverted it with `git apply -R`, so `git status` is clean.

All line numbers are at HEAD. Some failure output below was captured while the instrumentation was applied; there the cc test lines are 4 higher (`tests.rs:299` there is HEAD `:295`, and `:303` is HEAD `:299`).

## Verdict

The owner's idea that flaky tests assert the clock does not explain the known case. That failure is a race on **environment variables** shared by every test in the process. Tests that **leak env changes** into the rest of the run make it worse. One of the two flakes I saw in full-workspace runs does fit the clock idea: an integration test that, through its outcome, depends on a 200 ms production `lsof` deadline.

| # | Test | Class | Proven? | Seen without forcing | Severity |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | `compiler::cc::tests::terminal_formatting_shares_cc_keys_with_cold_and_warm_probes` (known case) | Env vars: a test reading without the lock races tests writing under it, plus an order-dependent env leak | **Proven**: exact hashes reproduced, interleaving forced | 3/40 `cargo test --bin kache`; 10/100 cc-module runs; 0/8 full runs | high |
| 2 | `cli::tests::test_is_macos_protected` (`src/cli/tests.rs:2823`, macOS only) | `HOME` cached in a process-wide `OnceLock` | **Proven**: deterministic cache poisoning | 2/40 `cargo test --bin kache` | high (macOS) |
| 3 | `sandbox_preflight_bypasses_denied_server_but_keeps_allowed_server` (`tests/fallback_recovery_test.rs:220`) | Clock: the outcome depends on a 200 ms subprocess deadline in production | **Proven** that a missed deadline gives the identical failure; that load is what pushes `lsof` past 200 ms is strongly supported, not forced | 2/8 full runs (one at ambient load, one under load I added) | high |
| 4 | `compiler::cc::tests::a_key_from_before_the_input_race_fixes_is_never_todays` (`cc/tests.rs:310`) | Env vars, same as #1 | **Proven** (forced, 10/20) | 0 | low |
| 5 | `path_normalizer::tests::from_env_construction_is_deterministic` (`path_normalizer.rs:2793`) | Current directory and env | **Proven** (forced: 11/15 via cwd, 4/15 via `KACHE_BASE_DIR`) | 0 | low |
| 6 | `compiler::nvcc::tests::execute_drops_artifacts_when_object_embeds_mapped_root` (`nvcc.rs:2299`) | Env var `KACHE_NVCC_PATH_NORMALIZE` | **Proven** (forced, 1/15) | 0 | low |
| 7 | `daemon::tests::detached_daemon_survives_sigint_to_the_callers_group` (`daemon/tests.rs:151`) | Inherited signal disposition (SIGINT ignored by whatever launched the tests) | **Proven** (deterministic) | 1 run, caused by how I launched it | medium |

## 1. Known case: `terminal_formatting_shares_cc_keys_with_cold_and_warm_probes`

**Location.** `src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:250`. The failing asserts are `:295` (cold probe) and `:299` (warm probe).

### Reproduction

- **As in `just check`:**
  - Command: `./scripts/with-test-resources.sh cargo test -q --bin kache`, 16 threads.
  - Load: 18 to 123.
  - Result: **3/40 runs failed** (runs 19, 25 and 39, at loads 21.6, 25.3 and 31.0).
- **cc module only:**
  - Command: `env -u OUT_DIR <bin> compiler::cc::tests --skip zz_flaky`, 16 threads.
  - Load: 58 to 21.
  - Result: **10/100 failed**.
- **Full workspace:** the `just test` command failed this test **0/8** times. Among 4,460 tests its window is narrow.
- **Forced, test unchanged:**
  - Command: `env -u OUT_DIR FLAKY_TOGGLE_MS=1500 <bin> --test-threads=4 <known test> zz_flaky_sdkroot_toggler`. The toggler holds the lock and switches `SDKROOT` on and off.
  - Load: 53.
  - Result: **20/20 failed**.
- **Forced, deterministic (a hook inside the test):**
  - Command: `env -u OUT_DIR FLAKY_FORCE_SDKROOT=/tmp/flaky-sdk <bin> --exact <known test>`.
  - Load: 64.
  - Result: 2/2 failed, byte-identical to the reported failure:

```
thread 'compiler::cc::tests::terminal_formatting_shares_cc_keys_with_cold_and_warm_probes' (147842183) panicked at src/compiler/cc/tests.rs:299:9:
assertion `left == right` failed
  left: "6a5dd9ebc2a33d878f7a0ea2cb8942db35b71cc3b4bbf8aca8d1ea4a8d5ae4d7"
 right: "ec170f0d4c633cc97b1a38b9c75e0ee2cbe2781647e22b1dca0817e436d3899a"
```

An unforced failure (`cargo test --bin kache`, run 25) produced the same pair at instrumented line `:303`, which is HEAD `:299`. Run 19 failed with left `23e919aa…` and right `ec170f0d…`.

### Mechanism

1. **The cc cache key reads the environment at call time.**
   - `cc_prefix_maps` (`src/compiler/cc.rs:4389`) reads `KACHE_CC_PATH_NORMALIZE`, `KACHE_BASE_DIR`, `SDKROOT` and `OUT_DIR` for its memo (`cc.rs:4402-4411`).
   - It reads them again when rebuilding the maps: `cc.rs:4445`, `:4449`, `:4458` and `:4650`.
   - The resulting maps go into the key at `cc.rs:6933` (the `prefix_maps:` line) and `cc.rs:7108` (source paths).
   - The test never takes `process_state_test_lock`. It computes `baseline` once, then recomputes the key 8 more times, each run launching a shell-script compiler. That gives a window of tens of milliseconds.
2. **Tests that hold the lock change exactly those variables.**
   - `include_dir_digest_exempts_an_existing_sdkroot_directory` (`tests.rs:6976`) sets `SDKROOT=<tmp>/sdk`.
   - `out_dir_and_sdk_maps_follow_the_environment_and_the_normalize_switch` (`tests.rs:7962`) moves through `OUT_DIR=<tmp>/…/out`, then `SDKROOT=<tmp>/sdk`, then `OUT_DIR=""`, then `KACHE_CC_PATH_NORMALIZE=0`.
   - The lock keeps the writers from colliding with each other, not with this test, which only reads.
3. **Two earlier tests delete cargo's `OUT_DIR` for the rest of the run.**
   - `build_script::tests::a_symlinked_root_maps_both_spellings_and_a_plain_root_maps_once` (`src/build_script.rs:2685`, with `remove_var` at `:2701`).
   - `a_base_dir_keys_the_same_across_checkouts_only_in_remapping_flags` (`build_script.rs:2790`, with `remove_var` at `:2810`).
   - The test harness starts tests in name order, so these run before the cc tests.
   - I confirmed it under cargo with `--test-threads=1`: an instrumented copy of the key computation gives `23e919aa…` when run alone and `ec170f0d…` when run after either leaking test.
4. **The reported hashes map exactly to environment states.** The key does not depend on checkout location: running from the main checkout gave the same hashes.

| Environment state | Key |
|---|---|
| `OUT_DIR` unset, `SDKROOT` unset | `ec170f0d…`, the reported **right** (baseline) |
| `OUT_DIR` unset or `""`, `SDKROOT` set to any path | `6a5dd9eb…`, the reported **left** |
| `OUT_DIR` set the way cargo sets it (`…/target/debug/build/X/out`) | `23e919aa…` |
| `OUT_DIR` and `SDKROOT` both set | `5503f180…` |

So the failure the owner saw happened like this:
- `baseline` was computed after the leaking test had removed `OUT_DIR`, giving `ec17…`.
- During the loop, a lock-holding test had `SDKROOT` set, giving `6a5d…`.
- The cold assert at `:295` fired first.

I checked these and they leave the key unchanged:
- the current directory, `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH`, `CPATH`, `LANG`, `PATH` and `CARGO_MANIFEST_DIR`;
- `KACHE_CACHE_DIR`, `KACHE_KEY_*`, `KACHE_CC_KEY_PROBE` and `DEP_*`.

**Class.** Env vars: a test reading without the lock races tests writing under it. Run order matters because of the env leaks. Not clock-related.

**Fix shape.**
- Minimal: hold the lock and pin the four variables with `set_env_for_test` before computing `baseline`.
- Better, per AGENTS.md:
  - pass an environment snapshot (`OUT_DIR`, `SDKROOT`, `KACHE_BASE_DIR`, `KACHE_CC_PATH_NORMALIZE`, current directory) into `cc_prefix_maps` through `KeyCtx`;
  - have the test pin that snapshot.
- Separately, the two `build_script` tests should use `set_env_for_test` instead of a bare `remove_var`.

**Severity: high.** About 7.5% of `cargo test --bin kache` runs fail, and it failed the owner's `just check`.

## 2. `cli::tests::test_is_macos_protected` (`src/cli/tests.rs:2823`, assert at `:2848`)

**Reproduction.**
- **Without forcing:** `cargo test -q --bin kache`, 16 threads, failed **2/40** (runs 13 and 25, at loads 39.4 and 25.3).
- **Forced:**
  - Command: `FLAKY_HOME_POISON=1 <bin> --test-threads=1 build_script::tests::zz_flaky_first_protected_call_under_home_override cli::tests::test_is_macos_protected`.
  - Result: failed 1/1. Without the env var it passed 1/1.
  - Load: 32.
- **Toggler running alongside the test:** 0/20. The test body takes microseconds and finishes before the toggler first overrides `HOME`.

```
thread 'cli::tests::test_is_macos_protected' (149397471) panicked at src/cli/tests.rs:2848:9:
assertion failed: is_macos_protected(&home.join("Desktop"))
```

**Mechanism.**
- `is_macos_protected` (`src/cli.rs:6209`) reads `$HOME` once, on its first call, and caches the list of protected directories in a process-wide `OnceLock` (`cli.rs:6212`, read at `:6223`).
- `KunobiConfigGuard` (`test_support.rs:107`) sets `HOME` to a temp directory under the lock. It is used by `cli::login::tests` and `planner_auth` tests; `wrapper_config.rs:345` also overrides `HOME`. `cli::login::tests` sorts directly before `cli::tests`, so they overlap.
- If the first call (from a `find_target_dirs` test, which holds no lock, or from this test) happens during such an override, the rest of the run holds `<tmp>/Desktop`, and every assert against the real home fails.
- Not forced: the test's own read of the home directory at `:2847` could also land during an override.

**Class.** An env var captured into a process-wide static. Whichever test calls it first decides the cached value for every later test.

**Fix shape.** Split out a pure `is_protected_under(path, home)` and test that directly. Alternatively, hold the lock and assert against the cached prefixes.

**Severity: high on macOS.** Linux compiles a stub that always returns false.

## 3. `sandbox_preflight_bypasses_denied_server_but_keeps_allowed_server` (`tests/fallback_recovery_test.rs:220`, assert at `:320`)

**Reproduction.**
- **Full workspace** (`cargo test --workspace --no-fail-fast`):
  - full6 failed with no added load (load 83 to 16).
  - full5 failed with 32 `yes` processes running (load 199 to 255).
  - That is 2/8 full runs.
- **Alone with `--exact`:** 0/20 at load 175, and 0/20 with 32 `yes` processes.
- **Forced:**
  - Command: `FLAKY_LSOF_DEADLINE_MS=1 cargo test --test fallback_recovery_test -- sandbox_preflight…`. A temporary hook in `src/fallback/macos.rs` makes the deadline adjustable.
  - Result: 1/1 failed with identical output. The control run passed.
  - Load: 227.

```
thread 'sandbox_preflight_bypasses_denied_server_but_keeps_allowed_server' (152410921) panicked at tests/fallback_recovery_test.rs:320:5:
assertion `left == right` failed: fallback compiler error
kache: warning: fallback `/var/folders/wq/48xldn_s09x1lqc7t7m16q7w0000gp/T/.tmpEfsZdx/sccache`: exit status: 42; compiling directly without fallback

  left: "fallback\ndirect\n"
 right: "direct\n"
```

**Mechanism.**
- To find the sccache server's PID, the preflight runs `/usr/sbin/lsof` with a hard **200 ms** deadline (`src/fallback/macos.rs:57`).
- On timeout it returns nothing, so the preflight declines and the fallback compiler runs. The test therefore effectively asserts that `lsof` finishes within 200 ms.
- I timed `lsof` while the kache unit-test binary ran: 341 samples, median 70 ms, p90 89 ms, max 241 ms, 1 over 200 ms. That was at load 27 to 56.
- I shortened the deadline on demand; I did not slow `lsof` itself.

**Second suspected cause.** The test reserves a port by binding and dropping it (`tests/fallback_recovery_test.rs:259-261`) before the sandboxed server binds it. Another process could grab the port in between, which would produce the same output. Next probe: log what each probe step returns during a full run.

**Class.** Clock/timing: the test's outcome depends on a production deadline. Possibly also a shared-port race.

**Fix shape.**
- Test the policy with a fake probe; `sandbox::check` already takes a trait.
- Or have the test pass a generous deadline, and assert on the `sandbox_denied` event rather than on the fallback never running.
- Hand the listening socket to the server instead of rebinding the port.

**Severity: high.** It failed 2 of 8 full runs, one at ambient load.

## 7. `detached_daemon_survives_sigint_to_the_callers_group` (`daemon/tests.rs:151`, assert at `:208`)

**Reproduction.**
- It failed once when I launched the test binary with `( <bin> -q ) &` (load 27 to 56).
- **Deterministic:**
  - Command: launch the test through a Python wrapper that sets SIGINT to ignored, then runs `<bin> --exact <test>`.
  - Result: 1/1 failed after 60.35 s. With normal SIGINT handling it passed in 0.38 s.
  - Load: 76.
  - Output: `SIGINT never reached the caller's group`.

**Mechanism.**
- A non-interactive shell starts background jobs with SIGINT ignored, and child processes inherit that.
- The test's helper process (`:124`) therefore ignores the `kill(-group, SIGINT)` at `:195`. It sleeps its full 60 s, exits 0, and the assert fails.

**Class.** A new one: inherited signal disposition, not timing.

**Fix.** Reset SIGINT to default in the helper process before it runs.

**Severity: medium.** It never happens from an interactive `just check`. It would happen in any script or CI step that runs the tests as a background job.

## 4. `daemon::tests::detached_daemon_survives_sigint_to_the_callers_group`

**Test path:** `src/daemon/tests.rs:151`

**Verdict: NOT A FLAKE**

**Severity: low.** The failure requires the test launcher to install `SIG_IGN` for SIGINT. Under the supplied verdict definition, a failure caused by the launch environment rather than by an unmodified suite state is NOT A FLAKE.

**Claim tested:** The helper inherits SIGINT ignored from a parent that launched the test with that disposition, so the group-directed SIGINT does not terminate the caller fixture.

**Evidence:**

- The test spawns the caller fixture without resetting signal dispositions at `src/daemon/tests.rs:169-179`, sends SIGINT to its process group at `src/daemon/tests.rs:200`, waits for it, and asserts that the exit was unsuccessful at `src/daemon/tests.rs:208`.
- A normal direct run passed in 0.44 s at load `{ 14.78 29.15 46.69 }`.
- A Python parent that executed `signal.signal(signal.SIGINT, signal.SIG_IGN)` before `execv` reproduced the report exactly: 1/1 failed after 60.40 s at the same sampled load. This is a parent-launcher condition; it is neither instrumentation nor a state produced by another test.
- Failure output, verbatim:

```text
thread 'daemon::tests::detached_daemon_survives_sigint_to_the_callers_group' (153649148) panicked at src/daemon/tests.rs:208:5:
SIGINT never reached the caller's group
note: run with `RUST_BACKTRACE=1` environment variable to display a backtrace
```

- The canonical resource wrapper foreground-`exec`s its command on every path (`scripts/with-test-resources.sh:47`, `:53`, and `:79`); it does not set signal dispositions. CI also invokes the suite in foreground steps at `.github/workflows/ci.yml:124` and `.github/workflows/ci.yml:1402-1405`. My canonical unmodified full-workspace run passed this test.
- A non-interactive shell may deliberately start a background job with SIGINT ignored, but that is precisely the external launch-environment case excluded by the NOT A FLAKE definition. Nothing in the canonical command or CI creates it.

**Difference from the investigator:** I agree that inherited `SIG_IGN` is the mechanism and that resetting SIGINT in the fixture would harden the test. I disagree with classifying it as a suite flake or medium severity: the report's only failure was caused by how the investigator launched the binary, and the requested rubric explicitly assigns launch-environment failures to NOT A FLAKE.

- The finding 4-6 forced hooks are opt-in: with their `FLAKY_*` variables absent, the added tests return or the production deadline retains its original default. The diff applied cleanly to `991c836` and reversed cleanly.
